research_question: Can the owned 2010+ Databento Henry Hub futures history reproduce published natural-gas futures market structure before any confirmatory freeze?
search_scope: Pre-outcome literature review focused on high-quality findings observable with retained futures OHLCV and point-in-time contract definitions: maturity-related volatility (Samuelson effect), Henry Hub seasonal term structure, and seasonal futures-price dynamics. #271/#273 protected outcomes were not inspected.

sources.title: Bias and backwardation in natural gas futures prices
Seasonality in commodity prices: new approaches for pricing plain vanilla options

claim_map.claim: Henry Hub natural-gas futures exhibit a Samuelson effect: futures-price variability is greater nearer maturity than farther from maturity.
Henry Hub natural-gas futures contain material seasonal structure in prices and futures-return volatility.
Natural-gas term structure is strongly seasonal: winter demand tends to support winter-contract premia, while summer/injection-season structure more often reflects contango.

expected_observations: For same-date expiry-ranked outrights, daily log-return volatility should generally decline with greater maturity rank; M1 should be more volatile than materially farther ranks such as M6 and M12.
The maturity-volatility ordering should not depend on one isolated calendar year and should remain directionally visible across the 2017-05-21 source boundary, even if magnitude changes.
Calendar-month structure should be non-flat: contracts delivering in winter months should show systematic relative pricing differences versus warmer/injection-season delivery months.
Economically sensible nearby-rank definitions may alter magnitude, especially near expiry, but should not require relabeling OHLCV close as settlement or outcome-driven deletion of inconvenient eras.
disconfirming_observations: Maturity-ranked return volatility is flat or increases systematically with maturity across the full sample and major source eras.
Any apparent Samuelson ordering exists only under a narrow post-outcome expiry exclusion and reverses under nearby reasonable definitions.
Delivery-month relative pricing shows no repeatable seasonal ordering across years or major economic/source eras.
The findings can be obtained only by mixing official settlement with UTC OHLCV close semantics, using unmapped contracts, or hiding failed parameterizations.
